worksheets.title: Trigonometric Ratios (SOHCAHTOA) and Finding Side Lengths

fluency_questions.prompt: In a right-angled triangle with acute angle $\theta$, opposite side $O = 3\text{ cm}$, adjacent side $A = 4\text{ cm}$, and hypotenuse $H = 5\text{ cm}$, write each SOHCAHTOA ratio as a fraction:

parts.label: d
parts.question: Which side ($O, A$, or $H$) is always opposite the $90^\circ$ right angle?

fluency_questions.prompt: In a right-angled triangle with legs $5\text{ cm}$ (opposite $\theta$), $12\text{ cm}$ (adjacent to $\theta$), and hypotenuse $13\text{ cm}$, state:
Given that $\sin(30^\circ) = 0.5$, $\cos(60^\circ) = 0.5$, and $\tan(45^\circ) = 1$, find the unknown side $x$:
State which trigonometric ratio ($\sin, \cos$, or $\tan$) you should choose when given:

parts.label: a
parts.question: The Opposite side and the Hypotenuse ($\text{SOH}$)

parts.label: b
parts.question: The Adjacent side and the Hypotenuse ($\text{CAH}$)

parts.label: c
parts.question: The Opposite side and the Adjacent side ($\text{TOA}$)

application_questions.question: A $10\text{ m}$ ramp slopes upward at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the horizontal ground. Using $h = 10\sin(30^\circ)$ where $\sin(30^\circ) = 0.5$, find the vertical height $h$ at the top of the ramp.
A $4\text{ m}$ ladder leans against a wall at an angle of $60^\circ$ to the ground. Using $d = 4\cos(60^\circ)$ where $\cos(60^\circ) = 0.5$, find how far the bottom of the ladder is from the wall.

A vertical flagpole casts a shadow $15\text{ m}$ long on flat ground when the sun is at an angle of $45^\circ$. Using $h = 15\tan(45^\circ)$ where $\tan(45^\circ) = 1$, find the height of the flagpole.

A cable car in Cairns climbs a vertical height of $200\text{ m}$ along a cable inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Calculate $L = \dfrac{200}{\sin(30^\circ)} = 200 \div 0.5$ to find the length of the cable.

reasoning_questions.question: What does the memory aid **SOHCAHTOA** stand for? Write out the meaning of all nine letters.

When $\theta = 45^\circ$ in a right-angled triangle, the other acute angle is also $45^\circ$ ($180^\circ - 90^\circ - 45^\circ = 45^\circ$), making the triangle isosceles. Use this to explain why $\tan(45^\circ) = 1$.
reasoning_questions.answer: Because the two acute angles are equal ($45^\circ$), the Opposite and Adjacent legs have the exact same length, so $\tan(45^\circ) = \dfrac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Adjacent}} = 1$.

worksheets.title: Inverse Trigonometry, Elevation, Depression, and Bearings

fluency_questions.prompt: Find the acute angle $\theta$ in each right-angled triangle using known exact ratios:
State which inverse calculator function ($\sin^{-1}, \cos^{-1}$, or $\tan^{-1}$) finds $\theta$ in each case:
True bearings are measured clockwise from North ($000^\circ\text{T}$). State the 3-digit true bearing for:
Use alternate angles and bearings to answer each question:

parts.label: a
parts.question: If the angle of elevation from a boat up to a lighthouse is $28^\circ$, what is the angle of depression from the lighthouse down to the boat?

parts.label: b
parts.question: Turn $35^\circ$ clockwise from North ($000^\circ$); write the 3-digit true bearing.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Turn $20^\circ$ anticlockwise (West) from South ($180^\circ$): $180^\circ + 20^\circ$ clockwise from North.

application_questions.question: A $10\text{ m}$ ladder reaches $5\text{ m}$ vertically up a wall. Since $\sin(\theta) = \dfrac{5}{10} = 0.5$, what angle $\theta$ does the ladder make with the horizontal ground?

A person stands $20\text{ m}$ horizontally from a $20\text{ m}$ tall gum tree. Since $\tan(\theta) = \dfrac{20}{20} = 1$, what is the angle of elevation $\theta$ from the ground to the top of the tree?
A yacht leaves Sydney Harbour and sails on a bearing of $090^\circ\text{T}$ (due East) for $12\text{ km}$. On what 3-digit true bearing must it sail to head due West straight back to harbour?

From a $30\text{ m}$ high cliff look-out, a tourist looks down at a kayak at an angle of depression of $45^\circ$. Using $\tan(45^\circ) = 1$, how far is the kayak horizontally from the base of the cliff?

reasoning_questions.question: What is the difference between an **angle of elevation** and an **angle of depression**? Which line are both angles always measured from?
reasoning_questions.answer: An angle of elevation is measured **upwards** from the horizontal line, while an angle of depression is measured **downwards** from the horizontal line. Both are always measured from the horizontal.

reasoning_questions.question: Why do we write a true bearing of $45^\circ$ with three digits as $045^\circ\text{T}$ in navigation and aviation?
reasoning_questions.answer: Writing all true bearings with three digits (including a leading zero for angles under $100^\circ$) prevents misreading or radio confusion in navigation.
